round2_rule_applied_informally.acceptance: T 15, G 14, S 13 (S is 2 below the best)
round2_rule_applied_informally.band: NO - S has the shortest makespan by 3.4x; the build band needs T's ratio >= 1.5. Strictly the 'run S alone' clause asks for equal acceptance, which S misses by two tasks in one run each.
round2_rule_applied_informally.caveat: exploratory, one run per arm, not pre-registered; the pre-registered window remains the formal decision

findings: With Qwen3.6 on the V620s the GPU implementer is fast enough (median 1.5 min per task) that the CPU team cannot keep up: three CPU workers at ~5-30 min per attempt are slower than one GPU doing every task in turn.
Review costs 3.5x the wall time (S 0.45 h vs G 1.57 h) for one extra accepted task in this sample: most of G's time is review, rework and the lead fix, not implementation.
Against W3, the team improved by 54% throughput and one accepted task with the Qwen3.6 lead + ripgrep fix, but that improvement is dwarfed by what the same model does alone on the GPU.

Team makespan is tail-dominated: rework affinity keeps a hard task on one slow worker (w2-10: 70 min). If the team design is kept, per-task time caps with reassignment to the GPU matter more than average speed.
suggested_next: Repeat S and G two or three times each (≈2.5 h of GPU time) to see whether S's 13/16 vs G's 14/16 is noise; the per-task flips say it may be.
Test a cheap quality gate on S: S plus one review pass without rework (flag-only) or a review only when the visible tests fail - the review's value per minute is the open question, not the team's.
If the CPU nodes are to be used at all: as overflow for a queue that saturates the GPU, not as primary implementers.
reviewer_speed_fair: replay-11 (qwen3.8 with ripgrep): 109 s per review vs Qwen3.6 tuned 44 s - 2.5x; see qwen36-gpu-lead-tuning.json

lt-7-g.harness_flag: valid=false: w2-10 'implementer runs failed 4 times (rc -15)'. Root cause is not infrastructure: the implementer's own endless loop hit the scope's 8G MemoryMax and systemd's default OOMPolicy=stop terminated the whole agent scope; each retry reused the broken workspace. Counted here as an honest w2-10 failure. Fixed in 5f09c84 (OOMPolicy=continue), not deployed for these runs.

findings: Run-to-run noise for the same S configuration is 3 tasks (12-15): single runs cannot separate arms that differ by 1-2 tasks.
GPU review (G) does not raise acceptance over the GPU alone (S): 12.7 vs 13.3 on average, at 2.2x the wall time.
w2-16 fails in every run of every arm; w2-07 and w2-10 flip between runs in both S and G, i.e. implementer variance rather than something review catches.
In G the review sends work back often (9, 10 and 10 rework rounds) without converting it into more hidden-test passes.
repeats_2026_10_12.next: lt-8-gc: G + --review-budget=1 (one review, one unreviewed rework, no lead fix) to price the cheapest review; then the CPU-overflow arm per cpu-overflow-proposal.md if pursued.
